subject: paediatrics
title: Pediatric Adrenal Crisis: CAH, 21-Hydroxylase, and Salt Wasting

steps.tx: Autosomal recessive enzymatic blocks in adrenal steroidogenesis impair cortisol biosynthesis while triggering compensatory pituitary hypersecretion. Accounting for over ninety percent of cases, **pediatric congenital adrenal hyperplasia** (CAH) results from mutations in the CYP21A2 gene on chromosome 6p21 encoding 21-hydroxylase enzyme. Deficient cortisol synthesis abolishes negative feedback, driving massive ACTH hypersecretion and severe bilateral adrenocortical hyperplasia.
steps.say: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by 21-hydroxylase deficiency in ninety percent of cases. Absent cortisol drives ACTH hypersecretion and adrenal hyperplasia.

vis.alt: Clinical photograph showing clitoromegaly and labioscrotal fusion in a virilized 46,XX infant with congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
vis.caption: Ambiguous virilized external genitalia with clitoromegaly and labioscrotal fusion in a 46,XX newborn with CAH. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Blockade of the 21-hydroxylase enzymatic pathway diverts upstream steroid precursors into unchecked adrenal androgen synthesis. Accumulation of steroid intermediates behind the enzymatic block drives massive shunting into the androgenic pathway, generating excess **17-hydroxyprogesterone and androgens in CAH**, including androstenedione and testosterone. In genetically female 46,XX fetuses, exposure to high circulating androgens during embryogenesis causes intrauterine virilization of external genitalia.
steps.say: Enzymatic blockade shunts accumulated 17-hydroxyprogesterone into androgens. This virilizes the external genitalia of 46,XX female infants in utero.

rows: Severe salt-wasting + Incomplete virilization in males

steps.tx: Follow the blocked lane in this pathway and the whole syndrome falls out. A **21-hydroxylase block** stops cortisol and aldosterone production while precursors behind the dam flood into androgens, virilising a female infant and wasting salt in both sexes. The raised 17-hydroxyprogesterone above the block is the screening measurement. Treatment replaces the two missing hormones and turns off the androgen flood by restoring feedback.
steps.say: Blocking 21-hydroxylase removes cortisol and aldosterone while androgens flood upward. Raised 17-hydroxyprogesterone is the screening clue.

vis.alt: Diagram of adrenal steroidogenesis highlighting the 21-hydroxylase block and androgen shunting.
vis.caption: A blocked step in cortisol synthesis diverts precursors into the androgen pathway. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Anatomical masculinization of external genitalia in female neonates spans a spectrum from mild clitoromegaly to complete urethral penile transposition. Standardized classification under the **Prader staging of virilization** categorizes genital ambiguity from Stage I, marked by isolated clitoral hypertrophy, to Stage V, characterized by a completely masculinized phallus with a penile tip urethral meatus and empty bifid scrotum.
steps.say: Prader staging categorizes virilization from Stage one clitoromegaly to Stage five complete penile masculinization. In genetic females, ovaries and uterus are normal.

left.title: Prader Virilization Stages
points: Stage I: clitoromegaly without labial fusion
Stage II: clitoromegaly with posterior labial fusion
Stage III: enlarged phallus with common urogenital sinus
Stage IV & V: phallic urethra, complete scrotal fusion

right.title: Internal Mullerian Structures
points: Absence of testes means zero Anti-Mullerian Hormone (AMH)
Fallopian tubes, uterus, and upper vagina develop normally
Pelvic ultrasound confirms normal female internal genitalia
Urgent karyotype confirms 46,XX chromosomal status

steps.tx: Concomitant aldosterone deficiency prevents distal renal tubular sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion. In seventy-five percent of infants with classical 21-hydroxylase deficiency, the **neonatal salt-wasting crisis in CAH** emerges acutely between seven and twenty-one days of life. Male infants appear completely normal at birth without ambiguous genitalia, presenting late with poor feeding, vomiting, dehydration, shock, and profound failure to thrive.
steps.say: Aldosterone deficiency causes a salt-wasting crisis at one to three weeks of life. Male infants have normal genitalia and present with vomiting, shock, and hyperkalemia.

rows: Renal wasting of sodium from zero aldosterone
Reverses with volume and steroid replacement

steps.tx: Measurement of markedly elevated steroid precursors provides definitive biochemical confirmation in suspected CAH. Measuring serum **17-hydroxyprogesterone diagnostic levels** demonstrates dramatic elevations, typically exceeding one thousand to ten thousand nanograms per decilitre (normal below one hundred). Universal newborn screening utilizes heel-prick dried blood spots, measuring 17-OHP by immunoassay at forty-eight to seventy-two hours of life.
steps.say: Markedly elevated serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone exceeding one thousand nanograms confirms 21-hydroxylase deficiency. Universal newborn heel-prick screening saves lives.

left.title: Diagnostic Biochemical Markers
points: Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone (17-OHP) >1,000-10,000 ng/dL
Markedly elevated plasma renin activity (PRA)
Elevated serum ACTH and adrenal androstenedione
Low or undetectable serum cortisol and aldosterone

right.title: Newborn Dried Blood Screening
points: Heel-prick dried blood spot on filter paper
Optimal sampling at 48 to 72 hours of life
Thresholds adjusted for birth weight and gestational age
Identifies affected male infants before fatal shock

steps.tx: Acute adrenal crisis represents a hyperkalemic, hyponatremic, hypovolemic emergency demanding immediate intravenous resuscitation. Immediate therapy for an **acute adrenal crisis protocol** begins with aggressive volume expansion using twenty millilitres per kilogram of isotonic 0.9% normal saline with ten percent dextrose, followed by immediate intravenous stress-dose hydrocortisone (fifty to one hundred milligrams per square metre bolus). Potassium solutions are strictly contraindicated.
steps.say: Treat adrenal crisis with normal saline and dextrose boluses, followed immediately by IV stress-dose hydrocortisone. Never administer fluids containing potassium.

rows: 50-100 mg/m2 stat bolus, then divided q6h
10% Calcium gluconate (0.5 mL/kg IV over 10 min)
Membrane stabilization if ECG shows peaked T
Does not lower potassium; protects myocardium

steps.tx: Lifelong dual hormonal replacement therapy substitutes deficient physiological hormones while suppressing abnormal androgen hypersecretion. Long-term maintenance therapy utilizes **oral hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone in CAH**, administering physiological hydrocortisone (ten to fifteen milligrams per square metre daily in three divided doses) to suppress pituitary ACTH, alongside mineralocorticoid replacement with oral fludrocortisone (0.05 to 0.2 milligrams daily) and sodium chloride supplementation.
steps.say: Lifelong treatment requires oral hydrocortisone to suppress ACTH and fludrocortisone to replace aldosterone. Infant diets require supplemental sodium chloride.

left.title: Hydrocortisone Replacement (Glucocorticoid)
points: Dose: 10 to 15 mg/m2/day divided in 3 doses
Highest dose in early morning to blunt ACTH surge
Suppresses excessive adrenal androgen production
Prevents precocious pseudopuberty and bone age advancement

right.title: Fludrocortisone Replacement (Mineralocorticoid)
points: Dose: 0.05 to 0.2 mg once daily orally
Normalizes serum sodium, potassium, and plasma renin
Oral sodium chloride (1-2 g/day) added in infancy
Dose adjusted based on blood pressure and renin levels

steps.tx: During physiological stress, infection, or surgery, steroid clearance accelerates, necessitating immediate dose escalation to avert fatal crisis. Parents are instructed in **stress dosing rules in adrenal insufficiency**, requiring tripling of the baseline oral hydrocortisone dose during febrile illnesses or minor procedures. If persistent vomiting or diarrhea prevents oral absorption, parents must immediately administer intramuscular hydrocortisone and seek emergency medical care.
steps.say: Triple the oral hydrocortisone dose during fever or minor illnesses. If the child vomits, administer intramuscular hydrocortisone immediately to prevent collapse.

rows: Preoperative bolus on call to operating room
